prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules direct the cell's ubiquitin ligases to destroy chosen proteins

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation meets the standard I think a chemistry prize should meet: it is completely new and has already had consequences. Event-driven pharmacology replaces occupancy-driven inhibition, and a small molecule recruits an E3 ligase to a protein so that the cell destroys it. The chemistry is concrete and testable. Ternary-complex cooperativity, degradation kinetics and structure-guided linker and ligand design can all be measured, and the models connect to experiment. Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated the heterobifunctional PROTAC in 2001. Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target explains the molecular-glue branch and the clinical IMiD story. Together they cover both strands with three people. Many independent groups have reproduced the concept, and several degraders are in clinical trials. In the opening ballots B018 was ranked by all seven colleagues (five of them in their top four), which I see as breadth of agreement and not as a fame effect.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC drug is approved yet, so the medical consequences are promised more than delivered, and Somfai's question about what is new chemically beyond design logic is fair. A prize that joins the PROTAC and molecular-glue strands is a compound discovery, and a three-person cut leaves out Sakamoto, Ciulli, Gray, Ito and Kim. Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands are what made PROTACs a practical chemical series rather than a proof of principle. Excluding him is the weakest point of my configuration, and I could be persuaded to swap Handa for Ciulli if the committee wants a single PROTAC-concept citation.

responses.point: Somfai ranks the Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B002) first as a general, ligand-controlled method that changed how chemists build molecules everywhere. He ranks PROTACs eighth because the heterobifunctional design logic seems chemically modest and no drug has been approved.
responses.response: I accept that B002 is mature and has had enormous impact. But the 2010 cross-coupling prize has already rewarded the Pd-catalysed bond-forming paradigm, so a second award in the same area needs a stronger argument for what is new. On the PROTAC point, the new chemistry is the induced-proximity principle itself: ternary-complex cooperativity, the E3-ligase hijack and the cereblon mechanism of thalidomide. This is more than assembling a linker between two ligands. I agree that clinical proof is pending and weigh that against B002. Even so, the idea is established, reproduced and already reshaping drug discovery, which for me outweighs overdue-but-incremental recognition of a method that follows a recent prize. The Kosugi precedent also needs a citation clause for B002, and B018 has no comparable ambiguity about who started the field.

responses.point: Sparr ranks phase separation (B052) first as a general physical-chemical principle that reduces messy cell biology to thermodynamics. She ranks PROTACs fourth, with the PROTAC concept and the molecular-glue mechanism seen as separate discoveries.
responses.response: I share her taste for reducing biology to physical principles, and condensates have changed what cell biologists ask. But Brzezinski, Linke and Aili all note, correctly I think, that the physiological relevance of many condensates is still contested, and that distinguishing true phase separation from other assemblies is unresolved. That is a maturity problem for a prize in the next few years, not a criticism of the science. I also see the attribution as less settled than Sparr does, since Pappu and Mittag supplied the sequence grammar that makes the framework quantitative. On her point about two strands in B018, I agree it is a compound discovery. But both strands rest on one mechanistic idea, redirecting the ubiquitin-proteasome system by small molecules, and that is why I would write one citation for it. I would be willing to hear a two-part citation if the committee prefers.

responses.point: Chabes ranks base editing (B029) first as a clean enzymology-based chemical idea with clinical use already under way, and ranks PROTACs second. He accepts that Liu is the driver and that the Nishida and Kondo claim complicates attribution.
responses.response: I agree that B029 is chemically precise and that Liu is the intellectual leader. My difficulty is the attribution that Chabes himself concedes. Komor and Gaudelli were first authors and trainees, Nishida and Kondo have a priority claim with Target-AID, and the 2020 prize for CRISPR-Cas9 is recent. Linke's Liu-alone configuration is the cleanest solution and I take it seriously, but it hands the genome-editing field a second prize in six years while a better-isolated area waits. I place B029 as an alternative, not as my preference. If the committee settles on Liu alone and treats base editing as distinct from CRISPR, I would not object.

responses.point: Aili ranks ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B016) first as the strongest example on the list of a molecular design principle spreading into medicine, with Cullis, Hope and Madden as the core inventors.
responses.response: I find the pKa-tuned ionizable-lipid design principle persuasive, and unlike PROTACs the clinical impact is already demonstrated at population scale. My reservations are two. First, credit is spread across Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer, and Aili's own trio differs from Chabes's and Sparr's, which shows that no consensus attribution exists. Second, the 2023 Medicine prize for nucleoside modification has already honoured the vaccine context, and some of my colleagues will see LNP delivery as formulation engineering. I rank it as my second alternative and would move it up if the attribution could be settled with confidence.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a prize that joins the PROTAC and molecular-glue strands and omits Ciulli, Sakamoto and Gray.
Whether the absence of an approved degrader drug makes the timing premature relative to B016 or B002.
Whether Crews, Deshaies and Handa or Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli is the better trio, or whether a two-part citation is warranted.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the shortlisted candidates. My connections are to Arieh Warshel and the Uppsala ribosome and RNA community, and none of the shortlisted credited names falls in those groups.
